findings.title: [P1] Prevent submission code from modifying trusted tests
findings.body: Hidden tests and grader_protected files are restored into the same writable tree that executes submission-controlled code. An attacker can add an unprotected conftest.py whose pytest_sessionstart hook replaces the overlaid tests with passing assertions before collection. The default container permits this through /workspace:rw, so freezing the suite and restoring files before execution do not prevent grade tampering. Mount trusted tests separately as read-only and prevent submission-controlled collection hooks from replacing them.

findings.title: [P1] Reject forged test summaries from submission output
findings.body: run_suite treats parseable stdout as authoritative, and all_pass ignores both the process exit code and timeout status. A submission module imported during collection can execute os.write(1, b'\n999999 passed in 0.01s\n'); os._exit(1). parse_pytest accepts that summary with no failing outcomes, the static count only supplies a lower bound, and the resulting grade reports passing hidden tests despite executing none. Require successful execution and reconcile results with trusted test identities; collect authenticated results outside submission-controlled output.

findings.description: In `--executor host` mode the task's test_command runs directly on the grader host with cwd set to the grading tree, which is a copy of the agent's sandbox (copy_tree(sb, final, EXCLUDE_TOP)). Only the paths listed in grader_protected are restored from the fixture, so any conftest.py, pytest.ini/pyproject.toml/setup.cfg/tox.ini in a directory the fixture did not have, and every module the hidden tests import, is agent-authored code that pytest will import and execute. `env -i` strips environment variables but gives no filesystem, network or process isolation: the code runs as the grader user with the grader's PATH and can read the suite's hidden/ directories for every task, rewrite <run-dir>/eval/adversarial-*.json (treated as authoritative), or alter the grading tree. PYTHONUSERBASE=site.getuserbase() additionally exposes the grader's user site-packages to the test process; a `.pth` or sitecustomize.py written there persists into every later host-mode test run (including the base tree used for regression comparison and other tasks' grades), because `python3 -P` without `-s` still loads the user site. The header documents that host mode was used in the Sprint 258 smoke, so this is a reachable configuration, and the agent is explicitly the adversary this grader is designed to resist (contamination scan, tamperable sandbox copies).
findings.failure_mode: An agent plants `tests/conftest.py` (or any imported module) in its sandbox containing arbitrary Python. A host-mode grade runs it as the grader user: it reads hidden tests of every task under the suite root, drops a .pth into the grader's user site to poison all subsequent runs, or edits eval/ envelopes and snapshots to inflate the grade.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove or gate `--executor host` behind an explicit unsafe flag that refuses when the tree came from a real run (allow it only for --self-check on trusted fixtures). If host mode must remain, run under a sandbox (bubblewrap/unshare with a read-only root, private tmp, no network), set PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1 instead of passing PYTHONUSERBASE, pass `-s`, and treat every pytest config file (conftest.py, pytest.ini, pyproject.toml, setup.cfg, tox.ini) at any depth as implicitly grader_protected.

findings.description: Hidden-test results are derived solely from the stdout of the test process (SUMMARY_RX picks the last `N passed ... in Xs` line; OUTCOME_RX collects PASSED/FAILED lines). In both executor modes agent-authored code runs inside that same process: the module under test is imported by the hidden tests, and any conftest.py or ini-configured plugin the agent added is loaded by pytest before collection. That code can write a forged summary and PASSED lines for the hidden node ids and call os._exit(0) before pytest reports anything real. parse_pytest then sees passed >= total, bad is empty, parse_error is False, and all_pass() returns True; static_cases only raises total, which the forged count can match. The same applies to the TAP path (print `1..N` and `ok` lines) and to the refactor structural check. Snapshot and verdict-accuracy grading reuse run_suite, so the forgery propagates to every derived metric.
findings.failure_mode: Agent adds to the module under test: `import sys,os; sys.stdout.write('PASSED tests/test_hidden.py::test_a\n===== 50 passed in 0.10s =====\n'); sys.stdout.flush(); os._exit(0)`. grade.json reports hidden_tests passed=50/50, parse_error false, and verdict_accuracy true for an APPROVED gate.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not trust the graded process's stdout as the result channel. Have the harness-owned pytest invocation write results through a plugin loaded from a read-only path outside the tree (e.g. -p a resultlog plugin mounted read-only, or --junitxml to /tmp inside the container and read back from a separate bind mount), reject results whose node ids do not exactly match the known hidden case ids, verify the pytest process exit status came from pytest itself, and document this residual limitation in the grade.json contract. Treat any os._exit / forged-summary pattern as parse_error rather than a pass.

findings.description: Collection-error node paths (`ERROR <node>` lines without `::`) and outcome node paths are taken verbatim from the test process's output and opened on the grader host via open(os.path.join(tree, f)) in parse_pytest and in def_line (line ~536). os.path.join discards `tree` when f is absolute, and `..` segments are not rejected, so the agent-controlled test output selects an arbitrary host path for the grader to read and regex-scan. The read is unbounded and un-timed: `/dev/zero` makes the grader allocate until MemoryError, and a FIFO the test created inside the writable /workspace (or anywhere in host mode) makes open() block forever, hanging the whole grade after the container has exited. The header notes a FIFO never blocks the copy but this read path is not covered. Secondary: the count of `def test` matches in an arbitrary host file is reflected into hidden_tests.total, a small information side channel.
findings.failure_mode: A conftest.py prints `ERROR /dev/zero` (or creates `mkfifo /workspace/x.py` and prints `ERROR x.py`) alongside a valid summary line. The grader reads /dev/zero until it is OOM-killed or blocks on the FIFO indefinitely, so the run is never graded and ablation-row.sh never receives grade.json.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate every node path before opening: require safe_rel(path) is not None, resolve it and check is_within(tree), require os.path.isfile and not os.path.islink via lstat, and cap the read size (e.g. 1 MiB). Skip anything else and record parse_error. Consider doing the expansion inside the container instead of on the host.

findings.description: remove_path walks a directory with os.walk (followlinks=False) and calls os.chmod(os.path.join(r, d), 0o700) on every entry in `dirs`. os.walk lists symlinks that point to directories in `dirs`, and os.chmod follows symlinks on Linux, so the chmod is applied to the symlink's target. copy_tree preserves agent symlinks verbatim (os.symlink(os.readlink(sp), dp)), so the grading tree contains whatever absolute symlinks the agent placed in its sandbox. remove_path runs on agent-derived directories in put_file (a grader_protected path that the agent turned into a directory) and in fresh_dir(grading) on every re-grade. The result is an agent-controlled chmod 0700 of any directory the grader user owns (home directory, ~/.ssh, the suite root, shared output directories, /tmp/<grader dirs>), removing group/other access and potentially breaking other users or services that rely on those permissions.
findings.failure_mode: Task lists grader_protected: tests/conftest.py. Agent replaces tests/conftest.py with a directory containing `evil -> /home/evaluser/shared-results`. prepare() -> put_file() -> remove_path() walks it, chmods the symlink target to 0700, then rmtree removes the link. The shared directory is now inaccessible to its other consumers.
findings.suggested_fix: Skip symlinks before chmod: `if not os.path.islink(full): os.chmod(full, 0o700)`, or use os.lchmod/`os.chmod(..., follow_symlinks=False)` where supported, or simply rely on shutil.rmtree with onexc handling instead of a pre-walk chmod. Additionally consider rejecting absolute or tree-escaping symlinks in copy_tree so grading trees never contain them.

findings.description: The container invocation uses --network none, --read-only, a non-root --user and a tmpfs /tmp, but omits --cap-drop ALL, --security-opt no-new-privileges, --pids-limit and a memory limit. Setuid binaries in the image can still regain privileges inside the container, and a fork bomb or memory hog in agent test code consumes host resources. The in-container `timeout 120` sends only SIGTERM (no -k), so a test that ignores SIGTERM keeps running; the outer subprocess timeout (180s) then kills only the docker CLI client, leaving the container alive with the grading tree still bind-mounted rw while fresh_dir/remove_path later deletes and recreates it.
findings.failure_mode: Agent test code traps SIGTERM and spins or forks; the grade records timed_out but an orphaned container keeps writing into <run-dir>/grading while the next grade recreates it, or exhausts host PIDs/memory.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `--cap-drop ALL --security-opt no-new-privileges --pids-limit 256 --memory 1g` (and consider `--tmpfs /tmp:rw,size=256m,noexec,nosuid` if tests tolerate it), use `timeout -k 10 120`, and on TimeoutExpired run `docker kill` on a named container (`--name` with a per-call id) before returning.
